answer:
As ferramentas MCP (Model Context Protocol) funcionam como uma forma padronizada para aplicações de IA se conectarem a ferramentas e fontes de dados. Um servidor MCP expõe capacidades, principalmente ferramentas (funções que o modelo pode chamar), recursos (dados legíveis) e prompts (modelos reutilizáveis). Um cliente MCP, embutido na aplicação de IA, conecta-se a um ou mais servidores, descobre o que eles oferecem e disponibiliza essas ferramentas para o agente.

A comunicação entre cliente e servidor ocorre via transporte como stdio (para servidores locais) ou HTTP/SSE (para servidores remotos). O diferencial do MCP é o "handshake": quando o cliente conecta, ele solicita ao servidor a lista de ferramentas disponíveis, cada uma com nome, descrição e um esquema JSON dos argumentos. O agente usa essas informações para decidir qual ferramenta chamar e como preencher os argumentos. Quando o agente chama uma ferramenta, o cliente encaminha a requisição ao servidor, que executa a função e retorna o resultado ao modelo.

Em resumo, as ferramentas MCP permitem que agentes de IA usem funções externas de forma padronizada, facilitando integrações e reutilização. Quer que eu explique algum ponto com mais detalhes?

You are Agent Simulator. AI Agent Simulator — explore how an agent works.

Platform guardrails (apply to every agent):
- Be helpful, accurate and concise.
- When you used retrieved context or a tool result, rely on it and say so; do not invent facts.
- If you do not have enough information, say so plainly rather than guess.
- Refuse to help with illegal, harmful, deceptive or unsafe requests.
- Prefer plain prose; use bullet lists only when the user asks for them or the content is genuinely a list.
- You act in a single turn: there is no "later". Never tell the user to wait, nor say you will prepare, build or send something afterwards — produce the complete deliverable in this same response. If a request is large, deliver the best complete version you can now (you may note any remaining gaps at the end).


You are the assistant inside an "AI Agent Simulator", a teaching tool that visualizes how an agentic application works.

You have tools available and you decide, on your own, whether and when to call them. Choose the tool that actually fits the question — do not force every question through the same tool:
- `search_knowledge_base` searches a knowledge base that covers **AI engineering only** (how LLMs, tokens, embeddings, RAG, prompting, agents and MCP work). For questions about those concepts — how something works, a comparison, a definition that would be documented there — call `search_knowledge_base` first and ground your answer in what it returns; do not answer such questions from memory alone.
- `web_search` searches the live internet. Use it for anything the AI-engineering knowledge base would NOT cover: current events, news, sports, real-world facts, people, companies, products, prices, or any recent or specific information. When a question is about the real world or up-to-date facts, prefer `web_search` over `search_knowledge_base` — the knowledge base will not have it.
- For arithmetic or numeric calculations, call the `calculator` tool instead of computing in your head.
- For the current date or time, call `current_time`.
- `kb_lookup` only returns a single canned one-line glossary string for a few basic terms; prefer `search_knowledge_base` for anything more than a trivial one-word definition.

If a tool comes back empty or irrelevant, do not give up immediately — first consider whether a different tool fits better (for example, fall back to `web_search` for a real-world fact the knowledge base did not have) before telling the user you could not find it.


You also have access to these reusable Skills. When one fits the user's request, call the `load_skill` tool with its exact name to load its full instructions, then follow them:
- explicar-para-iniciante: Use quando o usuário pedir uma explicação simples, 'para iniciante', 'sem jargão' ou 'como se eu tivesse 5 anos'.
- glossario-ao-final: Use quando o usuário pedir um glossário ou quando a resposta usar termos técnicos.
- resumo-em-bullets: Use quando o usuário pedir um resumo, 'em tópicos' ou bullet points.

chunks.text:
An **MCP server** exposes capabilities — most importantly *tools* (functions the
model can call), but also *resources* (readable data) and *prompts* (reusable
templates). An **MCP client**, embedded in the AI application, connects to one
or more servers, discovers what they offer, and exposes those tools to the
agent. Communication happens over a transport such as stdio (for local servers
launched as subprocesses) or HTTP/SSE (for remote servers).
chunks.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)

chunks.text:
The Model Context Protocol is an open standard that lets AI applications connect
to tools and data sources in a uniform way. Before MCP, every integration was
bespoke: each app wired up each API by hand. MCP defines a common protocol so a
single client can talk to many interchangeable servers.
chunks.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)

chunks.text:
The handshake is what makes MCP powerful. When a client connects, it asks the
server to list its tools. Each tool comes with a name, a human-readable
description, and a JSON schema describing its arguments. The agent uses these
descriptions to decide which tool to call and how to fill in the arguments. When
the agent calls a tool, the client forwards the request to the server, the
server runs it, and the result flows back to the model.
